analyst_view.overall: Early view: Olympiacos (6th, 10 points) have conceded once in four league-phase games and are second in the Greek league with four goals against in nine games. Milan are flying in Serie A under Ruben Amorim (3-1 in the derby, then 2-1 against Genoa, five points off the top) but are 28th in Europe after three defeats in four, so this is close to a must-win for them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean lower: Olympiacos's four European games have produced five goals in total (2-1, 1-0, 1-0, 0-0), and Milan have failed to score in three of their four. Milan's domestic form is a warning, but in this competition both sides point to a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Milan need the points and will have to come forward, which could add corners at one end, but Olympiacos at home are used to managing games and giving little away, so the two effects roughly cancel.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean higher: Piraeus is a hostile place for visitors, Milan are under real pressure in this competition, and they finished with ten men in their 3-0 loss at Bournemouth. A tense, low-scoring game usually brings more fouls and bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Milan's need to win should lift their output, while Olympiacos tend to keep games under control, so I'd stay close to 24 or 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Milan have scored in only one of four European games and Amorim admitted they 'gifted opportunities' against Ferencvaros, while Olympiacos have let in one goal. Clear chances should be scarce; I'd expect around 7.
